title: Natural Resources
meta: Lean and continuous improvement for Canadian mining, forestry and resource companies: cut costs, clear maintenance backlogs and improve delivery and margins.
h1: Lower costs and steadier delivery for resource operations
lead: Resource companies balance development, use and protection under constant price and demand swings. We help you cut waste, clear maintenance backlogs and plan your workforce so operations stay safe, responsive and profitable.
intro: How do you stay competitive with finite resources?

Mining, forestry, aggregates and other resource operations face volatile markets, remote sites, tight labour pools and rising expectations on safety and environmental stewardship. Chmltech finds the places in your organization where you can accelerate performance, reduce costs and improve both delivery and margins. Our immersive approach brings together operations, maintenance and management to build practical workforce plans, sound maintenance scheduling and better communication across sites. We start by stabilizing the basics, such as clearing the backlog, and then put scalable processes in place that support future growth.
signs: Maintenance backlog keeps rising and equipment availability suffers
Crews wait on parts, equipment or instructions at the start of shifts
You cannot react quickly when commodity prices or demand shift
Safety, maintenance and production plans live in separate silos
Remote sites and head office work from different information
challenges: Commodity price and demand swings mean operations must scale up or down quickly without losing control of cost or safety.
Deferred maintenance on mobile and fixed equipment drives breakdowns, lowers availability and pushes crews into reactive work.
Skilled trades are hard to find and retain, and rosters, skills and workloads are rarely planned together.
Information moves slowly between remote sites, contractors and head office, so decisions are made on stale data.
services: We build a workforce planning model that links resource utilization, maintenance scheduling, skills development and communication across the organization.
We help you triage and resolve the underlying maintenance backlog, then put a planning and scheduling process in place that keeps it under control.
We define metrics for service levels, productivity, speed and quality, set the baseline and track results against an agreed ROI target.
Process mapping, data analysis and direct field observation separate value-added from non-value-added work and reveal hidden capacity.
Introductory process improvement workshops give your crews and supervisors the concepts and the change process they need to lead improvement.
A complete 5S assessment of shops, warehouses and work areas, based on Lean and Six Sigma, to remove clutter and create a safer, more efficient workplace.

steps.label: Truck breaks down
steps.text: A haul truck stops in the pit, taking production capacity with it.

steps.label: Report the failure
steps.text: The operator radios dispatch and a work order is raised.

steps.label: Diagnose the fault
steps.text: A mechanic diagnoses the fault and lists the parts needed.

steps.label: Plan the repair
steps.text: Planning confirms the job, labour and parts, and books the bay.

steps.label: Find and issue parts
steps.text: Stores searches for the parts. Critical spares are often out of stock or in the wrong location, so the truck sits idle.

steps.label: Expedite missing part
steps.text: Missing parts are rush-ordered from the supplier at premium freight, then the job returns to the stores queue.

steps.label: Repair and test
steps.text: The crew repairs the truck and tests it before release.

steps.label: Back in production
steps.text: The truck returns to the haul cycle.

config.fix_title: Fixed: critical spares and parts kitting
config.fix_text: A critical spares list with min/max levels keeps key parts on the shelf, planners kit parts before the job starts, and planned component change-outs replace many breakdowns. Trucks stop waiting at stores.

examples: Haul truck maintenance at an open-pit site
Trucks waited in the shop while mechanics searched for parts and tooling.
Kitted parts and a weekly schedule let jobs start on time and trucks return to service sooner.
Crews lost the first part of each shift waiting for instructions and equipment checks.
A short start-of-shift huddle and standard checklists get lines running promptly and consistently.
Supply orders were placed by phone and email, which caused emergency flights for missing items.
A simple shared order and reorder process gives site and head office the same view of stock.
outcomes: A smaller, prioritized and well-understood maintenance backlog
Better equipment availability and fewer emergency repairs
A workforce plan that matches skills, rosters and workload
Lower operating costs through the elimination of waste
Faster, clearer communication between sites and head office
A safer, more organized workplace through 5S

why.title: Why Chmltech for natural resources
why.text: We help resource companies react quickly to threats and opportunities while keeping safety and maintenance discipline at the core.
points: Before the project starts, we agree with you the results it should deliver and how they will be measured, and we report against them.
We work on site with your crews, planners and managers, so solutions fit the realities of your operation and your people own them.
We stabilize the basics first, then put scalable processes in place so improvements support future growth rather than a one-time fix.
why.note: ROI targets are set for each engagement based on scope and baseline data. Actual results depend on scope, implementation and operating conditions.

faq: What types of resource companies do you work with?

We work with growing Canadian companies in sectors such as mining, forestry, aggregates and related services. The common thread is a need for safe, reliable operations and strong maintenance and workflow management.
How do you return value on the investment?
Value comes from increased customer value and the elimination of waste, such as idle time, rework and emergency repairs. We agree an ROI target and how it will be measured before the project starts.
Can you work with remote or multi-site operations?
Yes. We combine on-site observation and workshops with remote follow-up, and we focus on processes and communication that connect sites, contractors and head office.
Do you offer training for our crews?
Yes. We often deliver an introductory Lean thinking workshop covering improvement concepts and the change management process, and we can add 5S training as part of a workplace assessment.
